newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean military to keep share of Codelco revenues.
newsitem.headline: Chilean military to keep share of Codelco revenues.

text.p: Chile's civilian government has no plans to try to amend a constitutional rule giving the powerful armed forces 10 percent of state copper company Codelco's annual gross revenues, Mining Minister Benjamin Teplizky said.

The armed forces say the 10 percent rule is needed to guarantee military preparedness and arms purchases, and also because it lets them avoid haggling over their budget every year in Congress, he said.
''I think the armed forces do not want to discuss this year after year in the (congressional) budget committee, with all the uncertainty which that would imply,'' he told reporters for foreign media.
''The armed forces say they need this for procurement and for dissuasive power'' against potential military threats, he said.

Chile's former military ruler General Augusto Pinochet wrote into the constitution a rule that gives the armed forces 10 cents of every dollar of revenue at Codelco, the world's largest copper company.

The rule, which puts about $300 million into the military coffers in some years, applies even if Codelco posts a net loss and is one many privileges which the military granted itself before handing over power to civilians in 1990. Though he handed over the presidency to an elected successor that year, Pinochet remains army commander-in-chief.
Teplizky compared calls to change the 10 percent rule to calls to privatize Codelco -- not up for discussion.
''This is among the issues that is simply ruled out...an issue of great political importance and which requires special treatment,'' he said.
''It's Chilean society which will have to decide on this issue when the time comes, and it seems that that time is not now,'' he said.
